Democrat Scott Colombe has won election to the U.S. Senate from Mississippi.
According to a race call by the Associated Press,
narrowly defeating Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by just a few thousand votes,
Kristen Kaler with Mississippi Public Broadcasting reports Mississippi's Secretary of State
has called for counties to certify voter results for an official end to the race.
Mail-in and affidavit ballots around the Jackson area have now been counted.
Yvonne Horton, a county election commissioner,
says they have one more step before the full process is complete.
These numbers, as of right now, are unofficial numbers
because we have to come back together as a body, the election commission.
Everybody's signature get together, and it will be considered official then.
Now, the Election Resolution Board will certify all results
before it is sent to Mississippi's Secretary of State's office.
For NPR News, I'm Kristen Kaler in Jackson, Mississippi.
Nine members of the Kennedy political dynasty argue in a new lawsuit
that President Trump's plan to build a 250-foot tall arch outside of Arlington National Cemetery
would cast a permanent shadow over their relatives' grave sites,
fundamentally altering the experience for visitors.
Max Kennedy is the son of Robert F. Kennedy Sr. and nephew to President Kennedy.
There's a long procedure that would involve architects and historians and public input.
And all of that has been ignored in this case.
This arch is being constructed at the whim and whimsy of an autocrat.
It's a vanity project, and it's completely different
than the memorials that dot the city and that enrich the life of the city.
Max Kennedy is the brother of Robert F. Kennedy Jr.,
Trump's health secretary, who did not join the lawsuit.
A White House spokesperson said some members of the Kennedy family
are seeking to "politicize a structure designed to unite our nation."
A new federal rule requiring Americans and certain immigrants to verify their eligibility
could evict tens of thousands of people from public housing, including many U.S. citizen children.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports the measure targets families with mixed immigration status.
Immigrants in the U.S. unlawfully do not get federal rental aid.
But since the '90s, Congress has let them live with family members who do.
Housing Secretary Scott Turner calls that "exploiting a loophole"
and says it's not fair to U.S. citizens, especially since rental aid is deeply underfunded
and only a quarter of those eligible ever get it.
Housing advocates and other critics say the new rule could separate families
and will actually cost more.
That's because mixed status households get a smaller subsidy
than those where every member is eligible.
In its own analysis, the federal housing agency says
that will mean the same budget will help fewer people.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
A rebound for A.I. stocks lifted the U.S. market today.
The S&P 500 rose more than one and a quarter percent.
The Dow added nearly half a percent.
This is NPR.
Democrats in the Montana House of Representatives
have elected a transgender non-binary state representative S.J. Howell
as their minority leader.
State Representative Zoe Zephyr, a prominent trans advocate,
says Howell is the first trans non-binary party leader in the U.S.
Republicans dominate the Montana legislature
and hold all six statewide offices.
The Ebola case count in the Democratic Republic of Congo
is now over 11,000 people amid violence against treatment centers.
NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports.
About half of those 11,000 people who got Ebola have died,
making this the deadliest outbreak in DRC's history.
Violence in parts of the country has disrupted the outbreak response.
Just last week, militants affiliated with the Islamic State
burned down a treatment center near Brennan,
killing nearly 50 people, according to health officials.
Given the rampant spread, the humanitarian organization MSF
is urging the World Health Organization to approve wider use of Ervibo.
It's a vaccine licensed for another species of Ebola,
but not the one behind this outbreak.
Clinical trials are ongoing, but results are many weeks away.
There has been some good news.
The last of nine Ebola patients in Kenya was discharged this week,
starting the 42-day countdown to certify that the country is Ebola-free.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Black bears could be making a comeback in Ohio
after virtually disappearing in the mid-1800s.
According to the Ohio Division of Wildlife,
sightings have sharply increased since 2022.
More than 1,500 sightings have been reported,
mostly in rural areas near West Virginia and Pennsylvania.
Experts say the rise in sightings could be due to more bears
or more cameras capturing them.
This is NPR.
